lines: Eight-voice algorithmic sequence generator: instead of programming notes you pick the scale and set the algorithm, and it produces eight note CVs and gates plus four modulation CVs and gates
Steps the scale selection on each press, from scale A to scale B to both scales stacked an octave apart and back
Changes the scale selection: a rising edge past 2V flips between A and B, or a high voltage picks B and a low one picks A, depending on the menu setting
Raises every note taken from scale A by one octave
Raises every note taken from scale B by one octave
Any voltage above 0V here raises every note taken from scale A by one octave, as the switch beside it does when it is up
Any voltage above 0V here raises every note taken from scale B by one octave, as the switch beside it does when it is up
While this is on, changing the scale A preset overwrites the twelve note buttons of scale A; turn it off to keep edits you make by hand
While this is on, changing the scale B preset overwrites the twelve note buttons of scale B; turn it off to keep edits you make by hand
Picks one of sixteen five-note presets for scale A, stepping from 1 to 16; it changes nothing until the preset switch beside it is on
Picks one of sixteen five-note presets for scale B, stepping from 1 to 16; it changes nothing until the preset switch beside it is on
Moves the scale A preset selection after being added to the knob, 10V covering all sixteen presets
Moves the scale B preset selection after being added to the knob, 10V covering all sixteen presets
Puts that note into scale A, or takes it out; the generator picks only from the notes that are in
Puts that note into scale B, or takes it out; the generator picks only from the notes that are in
Sets the internal clock, from 32 BPM at the left to 2048 BPM at the right; it has no effect while a cable is in the clock input
Adds to the internal clock tempo, 10V covering the whole span from 32 BPM to 2048 BPM
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it wraps and fires the reset output, 1 to 64
Moves the sequence length after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 1 to 64 span
Transposes every note CV, -3V to +3V at a volt per octave
Transposes every note CV, added volt for volt to the knob at a volt per octave with no scaling
Sets the note gate length as a fraction of one step, 0.01 to 2, so a setting of 1 holds the gate for a whole step; the maker's tooltip prints the value in seconds
Moves the gate length after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0.01 to 2 span
Sets how many of the eight voices produce gates, 1 to 8; the note CV outputs above the count keep moving but their gates stay low
Moves the voice count after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 1 to 8 span
Delays each voice's gate a little further than the one before it, spreading a chord into a strum across up to one step
Moves the strum amount after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole span
Sets the divisors and phases of the eight internal tracks whose on and off states the notes are built from, stepping from 0 to 127
Moves the algorithm X value after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0 to 127 span
Picks which of the eight internal tracks feed each voice's note and which of sixteen gate patterns is used, stepping from 0 to 127
Moves the algorithm Y value after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0 to 127 span
Steps each voice along the scale by this many notes, 0 to 12; above 6 each voice is shifted one step further than the one before it, fanning the voices apart
Moves the scale shift after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0 to 12 span
Sets how often a voice is silenced and for how many steps, 0 to 16, thinning the sequence as it is raised
Moves the silence amount after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0 to 16 span
Reads each voice further back through the last eight steps, -8 to +8, so the voices play the same material against itself in time
Moves the rotation after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole -8 to +8 span
Feeds the module's own note CV outputs back into its algorithm controls, 0 to 127; the higher it goes the more controls it reaches
Moves the cross modulation after being added to the knob, 10V covering the whole 0 to 127 span
A rising edge past 2V advances the sequence one step; a cable here stops the internal clock
A rising edge past 2V sets the sequence back to its first step and fires the reset output
A 1ms 10V pulse on every step, whether the step came from the internal clock or from the clock input
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequence wraps round to its first step, and on every reset
The note for voice one, as a volt per octave; it also carries all eight voices as an eight-channel polyphonic cable
The note for that voice, as a volt per octave
The gate for voice one, 10V while it is open and 0V otherwise; it also carries all eight voices as an eight-channel polyphonic cable
The gate for that voice, 10V while it is open and 0V otherwise
The first modulation CV, stepping in thirds of a volt between 0V and about 9.7V; it also carries eight modulation CVs as an eight-channel polyphonic cable
That modulation CV, stepping in thirds of a volt between 0V and about 9.7V
The first modulation gate, 10V or 0V; it also carries eight modulation gates as an eight-channel polyphonic cable
That modulation gate, 10V or 0V
Note — the module runs on its own clock until a cable is patched into the clock input, at which point the SPEED knob stops mattering and each rising edge is one step.
Note — the note buttons are the scale: with no note switched on in the selected scale every gate stays low and every note CV holds at one value.
Note — a preset switch left on overwrites the note buttons of its scale every time the preset changes, including when its CV moves. Switch it off after choosing a preset to keep edits made by hand.
Note — the two polyphonic modulation jacks carry eight channels each, although only four of the modulation voices have a jack of their own.
Note — six of the controls are only read on a step: the voice count, the two algorithm values, the shift, the space and the rotation. Turning one takes effect at the next clock, not at once.
Note — note CVs are clamped to plus or minus 10V, so patching a note output back into the transposition input cannot run away.
Note — the eight modulation CVs and gates are built from the same eight internal tracks the notes are, so they move in step with the sequence rather than independently of it.
Menu — Scale Switch Mode: Trigger, Gate — sets how the scale input works: a rising edge flips between the two scales, or a high voltage selects scale B and a low one selects scale A

SDOrcasHeartV2.notes: GATE_LEN_PARAM is configured with the unit " sec" at src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:373, but updateParameters at src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:446 multiplies the knob value by the step time before use, so the knob is a fraction of a step rather than a number of seconds; the control's line says so. SPEED is a 0..3 parameter displayed as BPM through a display base of 4 and a multiplier of 32 (src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:361), which gives 32 BPM at the left and 2048 BPM at the right. The two polyphonic modulation jacks are given eight channels (src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:706 and 707) although MODOUTPUTCOUNT is 4, so four of the eight modulation voices can be reached only through the polyphonic cable. updateSyncedParameters is called only on a step (src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:616), which is why the voice count, both algorithm values, the shift, the space and the rotation take effect at the next clock rather than at once. The twenty-four note buttons carry no lettering on the panel; their names come from configSwitch at src/SDOrcasHeartV2.cpp:212 to 225, and the panel prints only A and B beside the two rows. The maker's wiki (https://github.com/scanner-darkly/eightfold/wiki/Orca's-Heart-v2) agrees with the code everywhere it was checked, apart from being silent on the gate length unit.

lines: A meter that draws each channel of a polyphonic cable as its own line, up to sixteen of them
The voltages to draw; each channel gets one line, and nothing is drawn while the jack is empty
Note — a line is white for a positive voltage, red for a negative one and grey at exactly 0V. A voltage past either end of the chosen range is drawn black at the end it ran past.
Note — the module has no parameters and no outputs; the range and the drawing style are on its right-click menu.
Menu — Mode: Horizontal, Vertical — draws each channel as a line across the panel at its voltage, or as a bar standing up from the zero line
Menu — Range: 0 .. +10, -10 .. +10, 0 .. +5, -5 .. +5 — sets the span the display covers; on the two ranges that reach below zero the zero line runs across the middle

SDLines.notes: No family is written for the input: the module draws whatever is patched into it and gives the voltage no meaning of its own, which is the case STYLE reserves for leaving the colour off. Range and Mode are stored in the module's own JSON (src/SDLines.cpp:32) rather than as parameters, so neither can be clicked for help; they are written as Menu lines. The four ranges are the arrays at src/SDLines.cpp:21 and 22.

lines: Turns one voltage into eight, fanned out from it by a spacing you set, with a tilt that bends the spacing and a random offset per voice
Scales the input before anything else, from -1 through zero to +1, so a setting below zero inverts it; it comes up at +1
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to +10V after the gain, so the eight voltages can be produced with nothing patched in at all
Sets the gap between one voice and the next, -1.4V to +1.4V, with the eight voltages collapsing onto each other at zero
Chooses which way the eight fan out from the input voltage: downward from it, centred on it, or upward from it
Bends the spacing so the gaps grow towards the ends or towards the middle, -1 to +1 with no bend at the centre; the bend is scaled by SPREAD
Sets how much of its own random offset each voice is given, -1 to +1; each voice keeps the number it was given until a new set is drawn
Scales the SPREAD CV input before it is added to the SPREAD knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales the TILT CV input before it is added to the TILT knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Scales the RANDOM CV input before it is added to the RANDOM knob, and inverts it below centre; it comes up at zero, so the jack does nothing until this is turned
Moves SPREAD after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
Moves TILT after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
Moves RANDOM after the attenuverter above it, 10V covering the knob's whole span, and the total is held inside the knob's range
A rising edge draws a fresh random number for every one of the eight voices; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.1V
The single voltage the eight are built from; only the first channel of a cable is read
The eight voltages as an eight-channel polyphonic cable, voice one first
The same eight voltages as an eight-channel polyphonic cable, in the opposite order
Note — the random numbers are held until a rising edge arrives at TRIG, and they are saved with the patch, so a patch reloads with the same fan-out it had.
Note — fanning upward adds each voice's random offset, fanning downward subtracts it, and the centred setting spreads it either side of the voice.
Note — with nothing patched into INPUT the module produces eight voltages anyway, built from the OFFSET knob alone.

SDFormation.notes: No family is written for INPUT, OUT or REV: the module fans out whatever voltage it is given and gives it no meaning of its own. getCombinedValue at src/SDFormation.cpp:77 is what makes 10V cover a knob's whole span — the CV is multiplied by the attenuverter and by (max - min) / 10 before being added, then the total is clamped to the knob's own range. The centred setting uses a per-voice tilt factor built from tiltMin 0.255 (src/SDFormation.cpp:35) rather than the straight-line factor the up and down settings use. The eight random numbers are uniform 0 to 1 and are stored in the patch (src/SDFormation.cpp:144).

Note — the lamp beside a gate jack lights while that channel's gate is high, whether the gate came from that jack, from GATES, or from the all-on switch.
Note — a gate counts as high above 0V, so any positive voltage opens it.

lines: Compares one voltage against eight thresholds and raises a gate for each threshold the voltage has reached
Sets that channel's threshold, -10V to +10V, added to the matching channel of the LEVELS input
Raises only the gate for the highest threshold the input has reached, instead of every gate at or below it; it does that in the position the maker's tooltip calls Off
Adds to the threshold knobs, one polyphonic channel per knob in order; a channel the cable does not reach adds nothing
The voltage compared against the eight thresholds; only the first channel of a cable is read
10V while the input has reached that channel's threshold and 0V otherwise, or 10V only while that threshold is the highest one reached if the dot switch is set that way
The eight gates as an eight-channel polyphonic cable, one channel per threshold
Note — every threshold knob comes up at 0V, so on a fresh module all eight gates go high as soon as the input reaches 0V, which an empty jack already does.
Note — a gate goes high when the input is level with its threshold, not only once it is past it.
Note — in the dot setting at most one gate is high at a time, and none is high while the input is below every threshold.
Note — the lamp beside a gate output lights while that gate is high.
Note — where two thresholds are set to the same voltage the dot setting picks the earlier of the two.
